# Ashen Road

**This game began as an experiment. Not a single line of code or graphical sprite was created by a human: all code and graphics was generated by AI agents.**

A browser RPG with a top-down view and a procedural open world. Your journey begins in the
cathedral courtyard, where Sophos sends you to recover relics. Beyond its gates, towns,
traders, caravans, bandits and wildlife follow their own routines. Time keeps passing beyond
the screen. Play the introductory story campaign or explore freely.

The project is in alpha. It uses JavaScript ES modules, Canvas 2D and background Web Workers.
No game engine or bundler installation is required.

## Quick start

You need **Node.js 24 or later**, npm, and a modern browser with a keyboard and mouse.
Current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari are supported. Download or unpack the complete
repository, including `graphics/sprites` and `graphics/terrain/sprites`.

1. Open a terminal in the folder containing `package.json`.
2. Check Node.js with `node --version`.
3. Run:

   ```sh
   npm start
   ```

4. Open **http://localhost:4175/**.
5. Start a journey, create a world with the tutorial campaign, or continue a saved game.

There are no installable npm dependencies; **`npm install` is unnecessary**. Stop the server
with **Ctrl+C**. Opening `index.html` through `file://` will not work: modules and assets need
an HTTP server.

If the port is occupied:

```sh
# macOS / Linux
PORT=4180 npm start
```

```powershell
# Windows PowerShell
$env:PORT=4180; npm start
```

Then open `http://localhost:4180/`.

## First steps

Choose the new-world tutorial campaign to learn movement, dialogue, the library and combat
training with Sophos. He then sends you after an artifact. Returning it ends the campaign;
you can continue exploring afterward.

A regular new game skips the tutorial. The world seed determines generation. The start menu
does not generate a map until you choose a mode.

| Controls          | Action                                                 |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| WASD / arrow keys | Move                                                   |
| Shift             | Run                                                    |
| R                 | Draw / sheath weapon                                   |
| LMB / Space       | Attack while armed; aim with the mouse                 |
| LMB while unarmed | Speak to the selected nearby NPC                       |
| E                 | Interact, talk, gather or loot                         |
| Q                 | Switch between equipped melee / ranged weapons         |
| F                 | Mount your horse / dismount                            |
| I                 | Inventory and equipment                                |
| M                 | World map; town map available inside settlements       |
| J / H             | Journal / library                                      |
| C / B             | Crafting / contracts                                   |
| T / O / V / N     | Campaign / town projects / companions / world activity |
| P                 | Pause                                                  |
| Esc               | Close window / game menu                               |
| − / =             | Camera zoom                                            |
| F3                | Performance metrics                                    |

Press a window's key again or click outside to close it. Sheathe weapons in towns: guards
respond to threats and remember crimes.

**Debug mode** in menu settings enables map fast travel, instant timed actions and a button
to add one million gold. These features are disabled in normal play.

## Saves

The game saves automatically and through the menu. Saves live in the browser's `localStorage`
for the current website address, not in a file inside the project.

- Saves do not automatically transfer to another computer or browser.
- `localhost:4175`, `localhost:4180` and the published site have separate storage.
- Clearing site data deletes saves; private browsing may restrict storage.
- Regenerating a world or starting a new campaign resets current progress.
- Death introduces a new character; some consequences and belongings remain in the world.

If saving fails, check browser storage permissions and available space. Copying the project
archive does not transfer browser saves. Legacy display text is converted to English when loading;
unfamiliar generated names are romanized. Compatible saves retain their seed, map and progress.

## Project structure

```text
index.html                 Entry page
src/
  main.js                  Startup, controls and UI/world integration
  core/                    Simulation, world layers, routes and collisions
  world/                   Terrain, settlement and dungeon generation
  gameplay/                Combat, law, economy, quests, horses and other systems
  render/                  Rendering, sprites, lighting and terrain textures
  ui/                      Panels, conversations and styles
graphics/
  3d/                      Blender sources and model generators
  sprites/                 Game sprites and their manifest.json
  terrain/                 Terrain sources and sprites
tests/                     Automated checks and scenarios
tools/                     Local server, validation and build scripts
  previews/                Visual previews for assets and interfaces
vendor/                    Third-party code and required licenses
```

Versioned generation modules in `src/world/` preserve compatibility with older saves.
Game lore is embedded in gameplay modules; external lore documents are not required.
Repository text, game content and documentation use English.

## Development and validation

Run these commands from the repository root:

```sh
npm run check                 # Syntax, import paths, workers and previews
npm test                      # Main test suite
npm run test:compatibility    # Save and generation compatibility
npm run test:journey          # Additional gameplay scenario
npm run test:living-journey   # Extended living-world scenario
npm run benchmark            # Simulation measurements
npm run build                # Static game output in dist/
```

Run a single test with, for example, `node tests/combat.mjs`. The main suite can take several
minutes because some checks generate large worlds.

With the server running, open:

- [Character sprites](http://localhost:4175/tools/previews/sprite-preview.html)
- [Environment and riders](http://localhost:4175/tools/previews/environment-preview.html)
- [Terrain materials](http://localhost:4175/tools/previews/terrain-preview.html)
- [World generation](http://localhost:4175/tools/previews/generation-preview.html)

Artist instructions live beside the assets: [sprites](graphics/sprites/README.md),
[Blender models](graphics/3d/README.md), and [terrain](graphics/terrain/README.md).
Blender is needed only to produce graphics; players do not need it.

## Publishing

`npm run build` copies HTML, game modules, runtime PNGs and licenses into `dist/`.
Blender sources, tests and working documents are excluded. Deploy the contents of `dist/`
to a static HTTP host. Relative paths support subdirectories, including GitHub Pages.
To test locally, run `npm start` and open `http://localhost:4175/dist/`.

The workflow in `.github/workflows/` checks, builds and publishes `dist/` on pushes to `main`.
The repository's GitHub Pages source must be **GitHub Actions**. A local build publishes nothing.

Third-party credits and licenses: [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md).
